rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidates: chunk 0 line 7 "M5's session may still be running the re-send" and chunk 1 line 19 "the un-packaged session sits on the `m4/<slug>` branch" / "the packaged re-send sits on the `m5/<slug>` branch". "Packaged"/"un-packaged" are M4 and M5's own thematic titles (prompt keys `ae101-m4-take-task-end-to-end` / `ae101-m5-rerun-packaged`), so they resolve as arc-earned spine vocabulary; "the re-send" resolves under the module-arc-beats-in-openers carve-out (this exercise is Beat 1 of M6, opened directly in the M5 worktree per the session widget). No pronoun/demonstrative anywhere in the file lacks an in-file or arc-earned antecedent.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Only two backward-beat references exist: chunk 0 line 7's "M5 worktree"/"the re-send" and chunk 1 line 19's "m4/<slug> branch". Both name real, current prior modules (M4 and M5 of AE101 -- confirmed by the placement note "Beat 1 of the three-beat M6...directly after the opener" and the session widget's explicit M5-worktree continuation). No dead-beat reference of the canonical "the catch on the missing PR" shape.

Thinnest chunk is 2 ("Read the contrast, push back where it generalises", lines 26-31): 3 bullets, each a self-carrying move (skim past the opening plan; push back on unquoted generalisation with a re-run instruction; expect over-credit and close with a ranked list) -- not a wait-state or single context-dependent bullet. Chunks 1, 3, 4 all carry a prompt block or multi-bullet instruction plus their own content.

Closest call is chunk 1, "Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps" (line 17): the visible bullets (19-22) deliver the diff instruction, and the "rank the gaps" half of the header is fulfilled by the prompt block's own closing line ("End with: which gap matters most? Rank by damage-to-a-future-session...") rather than by prose outside the prompt -- but the prompt is part of the chunk's content, so the header still reads true. Chunks 2 ("Read the contrast, push back..."), 3 ("Cut one stale rule..."), 4 ("Say go, unless the cut spreads...") each match their bullets and prompt content directly; no header the chunk's own content contradicts.

grep -noE 'Not [A-Za-z].*\. Not ' on body lines 1-47 -> no output (no "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction). No anaphora/epistrophe triple anywhere (each bullet is a single independent sentence, not a repeated-lead structure). No self-grading superlative ("The point: two sessions are enough to place every lesson" carries a house stance, not a superlative claim of usefulness). No number-with-retraction ("three to five items" is a plain range, not a hedge-then-undercut). Closest abstraction-noun-stack candidate is chunk 1 line 22 "what new shapes of drift it introduced" -- "drift" is established AE101 technical vocabulary (not a vague coinage like "the bounded-window reality"), so it stays concrete. No verb-triplet-with-empty-leg construction present.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: All four `##` headings are imperative/phase-label, matching the exercise convention: "Diff the two sessions, rank the gaps" (17), "Read the contrast, push back where it generalises" (26), "Cut one stale rule the diagnosis killed" (32), "Say go, unless the cut spreads past the one rule" (41). None is a bare declarative claim (no law/consolidation moment is being staged here that would require the declarative override).

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: A bullet earns its slot or dies -- three classes that read as rigour and carry nothing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate is chunk 3 line 34, "Two sessions of the same task were the first real stress-test of `./CLAUDE.local.md`." -- reads adjacent to self-referential design commentary but states a fact about the STUDENT's own artefact's history (motivating the cut instruction that follows), not commentary on the training's own pedagogical design choice, so it stays a 'why now' tell rather than class (b). The half-life maxim at line 35 ("Rules-files have a half-life...") is the coinage, not a recitation: grep -rn "half-life" curriculum/exercises curriculum/lectures curriculum/trainings -> only this file's body line 35 plus its own backing-block claim row (line 95) -- no prior module states it, so it isn't the Nth recitation the (a) doctrine-restatement class targets. Every other bullet across all 4 chunks names a concrete move, object, or tell (branch/file coordinates, a re-run instruction, a ranking close, a go-ahead script, a scope limit) -- none is a pure aphorism kicker or doctrine restatement.

grep -noE '\[.*\]\(' on the body: no output (matches signals.has_urls: false). Body carries zero markdown links, so the cross-file-callback-by-position shape this rule targets does not occur. The M4/M5 references (chunk 0-1) name the source directly ('M5 worktree', 'm4/<slug> branch', 'task.md', 'plan.md') rather than locating it by position ('the previous module said'), so even read generously they don't trip this rule; that resolution sits under §1's carve-outs, not §2.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess-before-reveal construction anywhere in the body -- this is a diagnose-and-diff exercise (compare two sessions, cut one rule), not a live-demo beat that narrates an outcome and then asks the student to guess it.
